# pocketid_client (Resource)

Manages an OIDC client in Pocket-ID. OIDC clients are applications that can authenticate users through Pocket-ID.

~> **Note** The client secret is only available during resource creation and cannot be retrieved later. Store it securely.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a public SPA client (no client secret)
resource "pocketid_client" "spa_app" {
  name = "React SPA Application"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://spa.example.com/callback",
    "http://localhost:3000/callback"
  ]

  logout_callback_urls = [
    "https://spa.example.com/logout",
    "http://localhost:3000/logout"
  ]

  is_public    = true
  pkce_enabled = true
  launch_url   = "https://spa.example.com"
}

# Create a client with a custom client ID
resource "pocketid_client" "custom_id_app" {
  name      = "Custom ID Application"
  client_id = "my-custom-client-id"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://custom.example.com/callback"
  ]

  is_public    = false
  pkce_enabled = true
}

# Create a confidential web application
resource "pocketid_client" "web_app" {
  name = "Main Web Application"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://app.example.com/auth/callback",
    "https://staging.example.com/auth/callback",
    "http://localhost:8080/auth/callback"
  ]

  logout_callback_urls = [
    "https://app.example.com/logout",
    "https://staging.example.com/logout"
  ]

  is_public    = false
  pkce_enabled = true
}

# Create a mobile application client
resource "pocketid_client" "mobile_app" {
  name = "Mobile Application"

  callback_urls = [
    "com.example.myapp://callback",
    "myapp://auth/callback"
  ]

  is_public    = true
  pkce_enabled = true
}

# Create a client with restricted access
resource "pocketid_group" "developers" {
  name          = "developers"
  friendly_name = "Development Team"
}

resource "pocketid_group" "admins" {
  name          = "admins"
  friendly_name = "System Administrators"
}

resource "pocketid_client" "admin_portal" {
  name = "Admin Portal"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://admin.example.com/callback"
  ]

  logout_callback_urls = [
    "https://admin.example.com/logout"
  ]

  is_public                              = false
  pkce_enabled                           = true
  requires_reauthentication              = true
  requires_pushed_authorization_requests = true
  launch_url                             = "https://admin.example.com"

  # Only admins and developers can access this client
  allowed_user_groups = [
    pocketid_group.admins.id,
    pocketid_group.developers.id
  ]
}

# Create a client that accepts a federated (workload) identity
resource "pocketid_client" "federated_app" {
  name = "Federated Workload Client"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://workload.example.com/callback"
  ]

  is_public = false

  federated_identities = [
    {
      issuer   = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
      subject  = "repo:example/repo:ref:refs/heads/main"
      audience = "https://pocket-id.example.com"
    }
  ]
}

# Create a client for your own app that skips the consent screen
resource "pocketid_client" "internal_app" {
  name = "Internal App"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://internal.example.com/callback"
  ]

  skip_consent = true
}

# Create a service account: a confidential client that only uses the
# client_credentials grant has no callback URLs
resource "pocketid_client" "service_account" {
  name      = "Backup Service"
  client_id = "svc-backup"
}

# Create a client that accepts tokens signed by a key you hold, with no
# network fetch: Pocket ID verifies them against the public key itself
resource "pocketid_client" "signed_workload" {
  name = "Signed Workload Client"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://workload.example.com/callback"
  ]

  federated_identities = [
    {
      issuer            = "urn:example:issuer"
      replay_protection = true
      public_keys = [
        jsonencode({
          kty = "OKP"
          crv = "Ed25519"
          kid = "workload-key-1"
          x   = "yvYSrUQ7W-ZdbgGplSlqbqdVj8nDC074evhHLOUiKJM"
        })
      ]
    }
  ]
}

# Set the client's logos from image URLs
resource "pocketid_client" "grafana" {
  name = "Grafana"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://grafana.example.com/login/generic_oauth"
  ]

  logo_url      = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/selfhst/icons/svg/grafana.svg"
  dark_logo_url = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/selfhst/icons/svg/grafana-light.svg"
}

# Upload the client's logos from image files
resource "pocketid_client" "karakeep" {
  name = "Karakeep"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://keep.example.com/api/auth/callback/custom"
  ]

  logo = {
    source = "${path.module}/logos/karakeep.svg"
  }
  dark_logo = {
    source = "${path.module}/logos/karakeep-dark.svg"
  }
}

# Store the client secret securely
resource "pocketid_client" "api_client" {
  name = "API Service Client"

  callback_urls = [
    "https://api.example.com/oauth/callback"
  ]

  is_public = false
}

# Output the client secret (be careful with this in production!)
output "api_client_secret" {
  value     = pocketid_client.api_client.client_secret
  sensitive = true
}

# Use the client ID in other resources
output "spa_client_id" {
  value = pocketid_client.spa_app.id
}
```

## Logos

`logo_url` and `dark_logo_url` are downloaded by Pocket ID, so the URL must be reachable from the Pocket ID server.

- **Not set means not managed.** A logo added in the Pocket ID UI is left untouched while the URL is absent from the configuration.
- **Removing** a URL that Terraform set deletes that logo.
- A logo deleted in the UI is set again on the next apply. A changed image at the same URL is not detected; change the URL to refresh it.

`logo` and `dark_logo` upload an image file instead, so Pocket ID does not need to reach it. They behave like the URLs, with these differences:

- Pocket ID picks the image type from the file's extension and accepts files up to 2 MiB.
- The file's SHA-256 is part of the plan, so editing the file uploads the new image at the next apply.
- `logo` cannot be combined with `logo_url`, nor `dark_logo` with `dark_logo_url`.

## Consent

`skip_consent` hides the consent screen shown when a user signs in to the client for the first time. Pocket ID still records the authorization, so users can see and revoke it later.

**Not set means not managed.** A value changed in the Pocket ID UI is kept and read back into state; set it explicitly to have Terraform enforce it. A new client without it requires consent.

## Federated identities

A client with a federated identity can authenticate with a signed JWT (RFC 7523 client assertion) instead of a secret. Pocket ID picks the identity whose `issuer` matches the token's `iss` claim, then checks the signature, `sub`, `aud` and `exp`. The `subject` defaults to the client ID and the `audience` to the Pocket ID URL.

Where the signing keys come from is set per identity:

- **`public_keys`** are JWK documents (each with a `kid`, public part only) stored in Pocket ID. Nothing is fetched, and the keys are compared as JSON, so formatting and key order do not matter. Use several to rotate: list the old and new key, apply, switch signers, then drop the old key. Requires Pocket ID 2.15.0 or later.
- **`jwks`** is the URL of a JWKS that Pocket ID fetches.
- With neither, Pocket ID fetches `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json`.

`replay_protection` makes Pocket ID accept each token's `jti` once, and reject tokens without one.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The display name of the OIDC client.

### Optional

- `allowed_user_groups` (Set of String) Set of user group IDs that are allowed to use this client. If empty, all users can use this client.
- `callback_urls` (List of String) List of allowed callback URLs for the OIDC client. Clients that only use the `client_credentials` grant, such as a service account, have none.
- `client_id` (String) The client ID of the OIDC client. If not set, Pocket ID generates one. Changing it replaces the client. Must be between 2 and 128 characters and contain only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The client secret for non-public clients. Only available during resource creation for non-public clients.When specified, it must have at least a length of 16 and consist only of printable ASCII characters.It is recommended to leave this empty and let Pocket ID automatically generate a secret.
- `dark_logo` (Attributes) The client's dark-mode logo, uploaded from an image file. When not set, a logo added outside Terraform is left untouched; removing it after Terraform set it deletes the logo. Cannot be combined with dark_logo_url. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dark_logo))
- `dark_logo_url` (String) URL of the client's dark-mode logo, downloaded by Pocket ID. When not set, a logo added outside Terraform is left untouched; removing a URL that Terraform set deletes the logo.
- `federated_identities` (Attributes List) List of federated identities (workload identity federation) allowed to authenticate as this client. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--federated_identities))
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether this is a public client (no client secret). Defaults to false.
- `launch_url` (String) Optional launch URL associated with the client.
- `logo` (Attributes) The client's logo, uploaded from an image file. When not set, a logo added outside Terraform is left untouched; removing it after Terraform set it deletes the logo. Cannot be combined with logo_url. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--logo))
- `logo_url` (String) URL of the client's logo, downloaded by Pocket ID. When not set, a logo added outside Terraform is left untouched; removing a URL that Terraform set deletes the logo.
- `logout_callback_urls` (List of String) List of allowed logout callback URLs for the OIDC client.
- `pkce_enabled` (Boolean) Whether PKCE is enabled for this client. Defaults to true.
- `requires_pushed_authorization_requests` (Boolean) Whether this client requires Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR, RFC 9126). Defaults to false. Applies to confidential clients only — Pocket-ID coerces this to false for public clients (is_public = true). Enforced only by Pocket-ID versions that support PAR (v2.9.0+); on older versions the value is stored in state but not enforced.
- `requires_reauthentication` (Boolean) Whether this client requires reauthentication for certain flows. Defaults to false.
- `skip_consent` (Boolean) Whether users skip the consent screen when signing in to this client. When not set, the value is not managed: a value changed in Pocket-ID is kept and read back into state, and a new client requires consent.

### Read-Only

- `client_secret_id` (String) Identifier of the client secret currently tracked by Terraform, used to revoke the previous secret when client_secret is rotated. Empty on Pocket ID versions before 2.14.0, which keep only one secret per client. Resources created before this attribute existed do not revoke their previous secret on the first rotation; revoke it in the Pocket ID UI.
- `has_dark_logo` (Boolean) Whether the client has a dark-mode logo configured.
- `has_logo` (Boolean) Whether the client has a logo configured.
- `id` (String) The ID of the OIDC client.

<a id="nestedatt--dark_logo"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dark_logo`

Required:

- `source` (String) Path to the image file. Pocket ID picks the image type from its extension and accepts up to 2 MiB.

Read-Only:

- `sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the image file, computed at plan time.


<a id="nestedatt--federated_identities"></a>
### Nested Schema for `federated_identities`

Required:

- `issuer` (String) The issuer of the federated identity token.

Optional:

- `audience` (String) The expected audience of the federated identity token.
- `jwks` (String) URL of a JWKS used to validate the federated identity token. Cannot be combined with public_keys. When neither is set, Pocket-ID fetches the JWKS from `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json`.
- `public_keys` (List of String) Public keys, as JWK JSON documents, used to validate the federated identity token. No network fetch is made. Each key must have a `kid` and must not include private key material. Cannot be combined with jwks. Requires Pocket-ID 2.15.0 or later.
- `replay_protection` (Boolean) Whether Pocket-ID refuses a token whose `jti` it has already seen, so each token can be used once. Tokens without a `jti` are then rejected. Defaults to false.
- `subject` (String) The expected subject of the federated identity token.

- `source` (String) Path to the image file. Pocket ID picks the image type from its extension and accepts up to 2 MiB.

Read-Only:

- `sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the image file, computed at plan time.
